A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMAC research work. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–E, are available and readable; the text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original OMAC experiments on HumanEval, MMLU, MATH, MBPP and GAIA, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, optimization trajectories and computational-cost analyses.

after.justification: V5 retains the original benchmark results and experimental analyses in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Initialization, performance-based sampling, contrastive refinement and iterative joint optimization remain unchanged, as do the appendix prompt templates. Sections 3.1–3.2 describe optimization targets more broadly, including tool-use policies and memory management, but such extensions were already discussed in v3 Appendix D.6; no new operational component is specified.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval, MMLU, MATH, MBPP and GAIA Level 2. The additional code-generation and tool-using scenarios in Appendix C.2.6 were already present in v3; no dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: V5 newly states that Self-Consistency is included for arithmetic reasoning, but Table 3 still lists SE, LLM Debate, ADAS, AFlow and DyLAN, and no corresponding Self-Consistency result is identifiable. The reported comparison sets are unchanged, leaving an actual comparator addition unconfirmed.

E3.justification: Table 18 changes the stated GAIA metric from Pass@1 (%) to Accuracy while retaining every score. This is a limited revision to the reported metric designation, without evidence of recalculation or rerunning. Dataset splits, model configurations, budgets and other experimental procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The initializer/comparator ablation, hyperparameter sensitivity, iterative-versus-simultaneous optimization comparison, training-subset analysis and training/test curves are retained. V5's additional main-text summaries describe analyses already present in v3 Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three experimental repetitions and report means and standard deviations. The plotted error bars and their explanations are unchanged; no new run counts, seeds, uncertainty procedures or statistical tests are documented.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–18 and the results plotted in Figures 4–8 are unchanged. For example, HumanEval Fun-1.4 remains 89.25 ± 1.30. Table 18 changes only its metric labels, and the new Self-Consistency mention supplies no identifiable result.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2 and the positive/negative sampling construction remain unchanged. Neither version supplies new theorems, proofs or optimality guarantees; the broader descriptions of optimization targets do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: five functional/structural optimization dimensions, supervised contrastive optimization, iterative joint optimization and empirical effectiveness. The broader wording in the methodology does not establish a new central contribution beyond the scope already discussed in v3.

C2.justification: Applicability beyond prompts, task-specific efficiency considerations, sampling trade-offs and the rationale for iterative optimization were already discussed in v3 Appendices B–D. V5 summarizes selected points in the main text; the substantive discussions and limitations in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository, although Appendix E.1 retains the anonymous link. A new acknowledgment identifies TACC computational support. Experimental setup details, hyperparameters and prompt templates are otherwise unchanged; repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V5 adds the Wang et al. Self-Consistency reference. Its new Section 5 subsection summarizes gradient-based and non-gradient-based optimization distinctions already developed in v3 Appendix A, rather than introducing substantially new research positioning.

P1.justification: V5 revises scope descriptions in Sections 3.1–3.2, summarizes existing appendix evidence in Sections 4.2 and 4.4, and adds a related-work synthesis and acknowledgments. Publication and affiliation text also changes. These are localized revisions within the retained section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: All eight figures retain identical embedded graphics, and all twenty tables remain. Caption styling, spacing and placement change with document reflow, and Table 18's metric labels are revised. No figure or table is added, removed or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: V5 modestly improves accessibility by summarizing existing optimization validation, training-cost trade-offs and research positioning in the main text, and by clarifying the GAIA metric designation and code access information. The scientific method and evidence remain unchanged. The gain is limited by the new Self-Consistency baseline mention without corresponding results and the inconsistent code links.
